patch.summary: Partially update one existing writable clinical record
patch.description: Read the record first and supply its current opaque version. Requires clinical:read as well as clinical:write. The update is patient-scoped and never changes import_source or external_id. Omitted fields are preserved; a supplied null source_document_id clears only that link. A stale or unknown version is rejected with 409 before anything is applied, and every effective change resets review_status to pending_review.

post.summary: Resolve this connection's own external IDs to record identity and version
post.description: Maps a bounded batch of external IDs onto record IDs and current opaque versions for one writable clinical resource. Lookup is scoped to the calling OAuth client's own import source, so it answers whether this connection has written a record before and never discloses another integration's records or a browser-created record. No clinical content is returned, which is why clinical:read alone is sufficient. Call it before upserting to decide what still needs writing: a matching version means skip, a differing version means read the record first, and a rejected review_status means a human refused the record and it must not be re-asserted unchanged.

200.description: Resolution of every requested external ID

post.summary: Withdraw a clinical record this connection wrote
post.description: Marks a record as withdrawn by the integration that wrote it. This means the source is taking back a claim it made in error; it does NOT mean the record is absent from a later export. Institutions age data out past their own retention policies, so absence from a newer import is never a reason to retract. Scope is this connection's own import namespace: a record written by another client, or created in the browser, reports 404 rather than 403, because refusing by name would confirm another integration holds that identifier. Nothing is deleted, the identity stays reserved so an ordinary upsert cannot re-assert it, and the record stops appearing in lists, search, timeline, and clinical exports. Retracting an already-retracted record is settled as unchanged.

post.description: For photos and PDFs too large to pass through a model. Returns a signed URL to PUT the raw file to with the returned headers. The URL is a bearer capability that stages bytes of the declared content type and size once; it creates no document. Finalize with documents.upload_finalize, which verifies size and hash and creates the document. The content types, extensions and size limit are those of documents.upload.

put.summary: Idempotently write an EOB claim and its lines, pending review
put.description: For a claim the client read itself. Requires source_document_id. Idempotent on the importers' claim fingerprint across every source, so re-reading a claim a parser or another client already holds is unchanged, and a claim with the same number, type and processed date is the same claim. A pharmacy line may carry a fill (NDC or drug, quantity, Rx number, pharmacy, date): the server writes it through the fill write path, so the same dispensing read from a label, a receipt and this EOB is one fill, linked to this line. A caller without clinical:read receives receipts only.

post.summary: Answer a possible-duplicate flag on a fill this connection wrote
post.description: A fill written with review_flags [{code: possible_duplicate, fill_id}] may be the same dispensing as an existing fill. action same merges it into that fill: its evidence (documents, EOB lines, aliases) moves onto the existing fill, blanks there are filled in, and the flagged fill is retracted, not deleted. action different clears the flag and keeps both. Requires the flagged fill's current version (409 if it changed). Repeating a decision with the returned version is unchanged. Ask the person before deciding: a wrong merge hides a real fill. When the fill has more than one open flag, same needs candidate_fill_id.

parameters.description: The ID of the flagged medication fill.

put.summary: Idempotently create or update a prescription fill
put.description: Send the NDC (ndc) or the package chosen among candidates (ndc_candidate) with the fill, price, pharmacy and source fields; the server resolves the drug, never the agent. Provenance is required: source_kind, and source_document_id unless the source is manual. external_id is optional: when omitted the server derives it from pharmacy name, Rx number and fill date, or else from the source document and source_locator, so a receipt and a label photo of the same fill land on one record. The server links the fill to the patient's matching medication or creates one pending review. Returns the fill, the medication with whether it was created, and the NDC resolution (candidates when ambiguous). A caller without clinical:read receives receipts only, with no stored NDC or drug detail.

get.summary: The FDA drug label sections for a package NDC or SPL set id
get.description: Reads the FDA drug label (prescribing information) from openFDA's drug label endpoint on the server and caches it. Give the 10-digit package NDC (ndc_10) or an SPL set id. Returns the label sections that exist (boxed warning, indications and usage, dosage and administration, dosage forms and strengths, contraindications, warnings and precautions, warnings, adverse reactions, how supplied, storage and handling) as published, the label's effective date and version, and DailyMed / FDA NDC Directory links. status is found, not_found (no label is listed, typical for a discontinued product), unavailable (openFDA could not be reached) or invalid. Sends only the NDC or set id, never patient data.

200.description: The label sections, or the reason there are none

get.summary: Resolve an NDC against the openFDA packaging directory, then RxNav for discontinued products
get.description: Server-side and deterministic. An 11-digit billing NDC is converted to 10 digits by a fixed rule (split 5-4-2; drop a leading 0 from the first segment, else from the middle segment, else from the last), then checked against openFDA packaging.package_ndc; it is never ambiguous. A package openFDA does not list (openFDA answered not-found, not an outage) is looked up in NLM RxNav's NDC history, which still knows discontinued products: that answer is resolved with ndc_source rxnav and discontinued true when the product is off the market. 10 digits without hyphens have no known layout and are read as 4-4-2, 5-3-2 and 5-4-1. Exactly one listed package is resolved; several (only possible for unhyphenated 10 digits) are ambiguous and a person must pick; none is unresolved. The answer always shows the 10-digit NDC (ndc_10); ndc_11 is the billing form. Returns normalized drug fields. Sends only the NDC (and its RxCUI) to openFDA and RxNav, never patient data.

get.summary: Search packages by drug name, strength, form, route, labeler and package size
get.description: For a missing or unreadable NDC. Returns ranked candidate packages with the reasons each matched. It never picks one: show the candidates to the person, then pass the chosen ndc_10 as ndc_candidate when writing the fill.

detail.description: The missing scopes (space-separated when all are needed, |-separated when any one is), or the operation depended on.

ImportCounts.description: Counts only. Importer warnings carry free-text provider content and deliberately do not cross the agent boundary; the closed envelope is what enforces that.

ImportCreateResponse.description: An import job from an earlier AI import of the document (import_job), a document PHR's own parsers read (structured_import: a C-CDA or FHIR file imported directly, pending review, or a MyChart or EHI export ZIP staged for intake), or client_extraction_required (client_extraction): PHR does not queue AI extraction for a connected client; extract the records yourself and write them with the listed tools.

outcome.description: import_job: created, unchanged or retried. structured_import: imported (written directly), queued (a ZIP staged for intake), or unchanged (a ZIP staged by an earlier call, as it stands now).

payload.description: Optional corrected proposal for accept only; prohibited for reject.

range_min_inclusive.description: Whether range_min itself is within the range: true for a source's <= or >=, false for < or >, null when the source did not say. Changing range_min without this resets it to null.

range_max_inclusive.description: Whether range_max itself is within the range: true for a source's <= or >=, false for < or >, null when the source did not say. Changing range_max without this resets it to null.

LocalDateTime.description: Application-local datetime in the existing PHR JSON wire format; no timezone offset is implied.

MedicationFillUpsertRequest.description: review_status is not accepted. external_id is optional: the server derives one from pharmacy, Rx number and fill date, or else from the source document and source_locator.

medication.description: The medication-list entry the fill is linked to. Write-only callers receive the id and review status only.

medication_created.description: True when this request created the medication (pending review); false when it linked an existing one.

ndc.description: How the NDC resolved; null for a caller without clinical:read, who receives no stored NDC or drug detail. When ambiguous, candidates lists every match: ask the person which package is on the label and update the fill with that ndc_candidate.

MutationReceipt.description: Returned to callers that hold the write scope but not the matching read scope. Identifies the affected record without disclosing its contents.

NativeBackupMetadata.description: Asynchronous native-backup status without archive hashes, record counts, storage paths, failure details, or requestor identity.

ndc_10.description: Hyphenated 10-digit package NDC as openFDA (or, for a discontinued product, RxNav) lists it.

ndc_source.description: Which directory listed the package: openfda, or rxnav (NLM RxNorm NDC history) for a product openFDA no longer lists.

discontinued.description: True when RxNav's history says the product is off the market (its SPL marketing status is not active). Always false for openfda.

score.description: Ranking score; present on ndc_search candidates only.

NdcDrug.description: Drug fields resolved by the server from the NDC, with ALL-CAPS FDA values converted to appropriate casing (the raw listing is kept server-side). Keys are empty or null when the NDC did not resolve.

scope.description: Primary scope retained for backward compatibility. When scopes is present, all scopes in that array are required; when any_scopes is present, any one of them suffices.

scopes.description: All OAuth scopes required by an operation that has multiple mandatory scopes.

any_scopes.description: OAuth scopes of which any one suffices for the operation; the response may be a narrower projection under some of them.

access_level.description: The caller's own access level on this patient; owner means the caller owns the profile.

notes.description: Present only in patients.get and patients.create responses; patients.list omits it.

PatientBilling.description: Opaque patient routing and public identifiers only for billing:read without patients:read. Labels and access levels remain inside PHR.

PublicId.description: Opaque public id, unique per record type across this installation and unchanged by a native restore, which renumbers integer ids. Refer to a record by the pair (patient public id, record public id); integer ids are routing locators only.

summary.description: Counts only; no claim, provider, or clinical-record data is included.

format.description: zip: intake decides between an Epic EHI Tables export and a MyChart record ZIP.

import.description: What a C-CDA or FHIR document wrote. Records land pending review.

upload.description: A ZIP document's staged upload. Call imports.create again for its current state; an EHI export's source is confirmed and its proposals reviewed by the patient's owner in PHR's Imports page.

failure_reason.description: A fixed refusal or failure code.
